reference.title: Band Prone Incline Hammer Curl
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl up, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; step farther from the anchor, or choke up on the band, for more tension.
prescription.progression: More reps, a longer squeeze, a stronger band.

cues.text: Lie chest-down on a bench set to about 40 degrees, chin just over the top, balls of the feet on the floor behind. A rack stands under the hands with a band looped low round each upright; hold a band end in each hand, arms hanging straight down, palms facing in.
Breathe out and curl both hands up toward the shoulders, thumbs leading, upper arms still and vertical.
Squeeze at the top; chest stays on the pad.
Breathe in and lower slowly against the band to straight arms.
Short pause with the arms hanging straight, then curl again.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arms swinging back to help the curl
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms vertical and still.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the chest off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest on the pad and the neck long.
Keep the thumbs leading and the palms facing in throughout.
Lower all the way down each rep.

kinematics.norm: From straight to about 125-135 degrees at the top (clinical opinion)
Neutral (thumbs up) throughout; the hammer grip shifts work to the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023; Marcolin 2018).
Vertical and still, in front of the trunk line: the shortened-biceps position of the prone (spider) curl (Oliveira 2009 tested shoulder positions in curls).
Chest supported on the pad so the trunk cannot swing (clinical opinion)
Looped low round the rack uprights, so the strands run down and back from the hands and resist the whole curl (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a pull-up bar or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is heaviest at the end of the pull or push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Chest or neck discomfort on the pad: lower the bench angle a little or pad the edge (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Neck discomfort: rest the chin on a folded towel at the top of the pad.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbow with the upper arm in front of the trunk, where the biceps works hardest near the top of the curl (clinical opinion; Oliveira 2009 tested shoulder positions in curls); the hammer grip shares the work with the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bends the elbow with the upper arm in front of the trunk, where the biceps works hardest near the top of the curl (clinical opinion; Oliveira 2009 tested shoulder positions in curls); the hammer grip shares the work with the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Brachioradialis is strongly involved with the neutral grip (Coratella 2023; Marcolin 2018), and the hand grips the band.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Brachioradialis is strongly involved with the neutral grip (Coratella 2023; Marcolin 2018), and the hand grips the band.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm vertical as the forearm rises.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arm vertical as the forearm rises.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Stops the upper arm swinging forward.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Stops the upper arm swinging forward.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Hold the shoulder blades steady on the pad.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Hold the shoulder blades steady on the pad.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk on the pad.
